negative_experience.text: Abnormal vaginal bleeding after menopause in a 46-year-old female is a high-yield red flag for endometrial cancer; this finding should prompt immediate diagnostic workup even without other systemic symptoms.

Pelvic pressure, urinary urgency, and dyspareunia in a patient with a pelvic mass raise suspicion of malignancy, but absence of weight loss, fatigue, or night sweats does not rule it out; these symptoms are not specific to benign leiomyoma and should not be used to dismiss malignancy without imaging or biopsy.

Postmenopausal vaginal bleeding combined with hirsutism and bloating supports endometrial cancer because late-onset hirsutism with virilization signs may indicate ovarian or adrenal tumors, but in this context, the bleeding pattern and associated symptoms point toward endometrial pathology; do not apply this when symptoms are confined to early-onset hirsutism without other virilization signs or when bleeding is absent.
